answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work instead of account count. Each identity accumulates a persistent, non-transferable record of attestations and fulfilled contracts, like pigment layered over seasons in an orchard. Minting a thousand new identities starts each one bare as an empty field, while established agents carry a velvet-smooth, audited history that counterparties weight heavily - so fakes earn no trust dividend, no matter how many are spawned.
